full_judgment: 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated that the plaintiff case in short is that the defendant by virtue of kabala Nos. 9979 and 5580 both dated 19-3-1979 and sale deed Nos. 10088, 10195 and 10223 dated 20-3-1979 became owner in respect of 37.68 decimals of land out of 6258 decimals of land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 45, CS Plot No. 187, corresponding to CS Khatian No. 146, RS Plot Nos. 829 and 837 and has been in possession thereof. The defendant being in need of money, proposed to sell the Shop No. 3 measuring an area 90 square feet on the second floor of a building situated on aforesaid land and proportionate undivided and un-demarcated land covering an area of 005.97 Ajutangsha out of 5010 Ajutangsha the plaintiff being intended to purchase the said shop. Proposed the defendant for consideration for Taka 2,00,000 (two lakh), being agreed, the plaintiff upon receipt of Taka 35,000 executed and registered an agreement on 16-8-2010. It has been further alleged that the defendant on 16-3-2011 received Taka 60,000 from the plaintiff and acknowledged the receipt thereof by signing on the last page of the agreement. The defendant received an amount of Taka 5,000 (five thousand) on 14-6-2011 and further an amount of Taka 5,000 (five thousand) on 20-6-2011 and thereby the defendant received in total Taka 1,45,000 (one lakh forty five thousand). On 14-7-2011 the plaintiff requested the defendant to execute and register the sale deed upon receipt of the balance consideration money but the defendant delayed different plea and ultimately, on 10-8-2011 refused to execute and register the sale deed in terms of the agreement dated 16-8-2010. Therefore, the plaintiff issued legal notice on 14-8-2011 through his Advocate but the defendant did not reply thereof, hence, the plaintiff filed the suit with the averment that the plaintiff is ready to deposit the balance consideration money as order by this Court.
